chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abdul Hameed ibn Abu Ja'far Al-Farra', who said:

Indeed, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) had a tooth from his teeth fall out, so he placed it in his palm, then said: 'The Praise is for Allah.' Then he said: 'O Ja'far! When I die and you bury me, bury it with me.' Then he remained for a while, then another one fell out as well. So he placed it upon his palm, then said: 'The Praise is for Allah. O Ja'far! When I die, bury it with me.'

key_terms.ضِرْسٌ: a tooth (specifically a molar or premolar)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Abu Ja'far instruct regarding the burial of his fallen teeth?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the noble character of Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) by demonstrating his consistent gratitude (*shukr*) for minor bodily changes, viewing even the loss of a tooth as a sign of Allah's power. The specific instruction to bury the tooth with him reflects a unique personal tradition (*sunna*) among the Imams, emphasizing the sanctity of the body and the continuity of the self in the grave. It serves as a practical lesson for Shia believers to maintain composure and thankfulness during physical ailments or aging.
